questions.question: How does Professor Shiller describe the relationship between Economics 251 (Financial Theory) and Economics 252 (Financial Markets)?
options: They are strictly divided into theory and practice respectively.
They are self-contained courses that may have some repetition.
Students must take both to understand the subject matter.
Economics 252 is a prerequisite for Economics 251.
questions.answer: They are self-contained courses that may have some repetition.
questions.explanation: The professor states that they are self-contained courses and that they decided to divide the subject matter imperfectly, leading to some repetition.
questions.flashcard_back: Yes, they are self-contained, though there may be some repetition between them.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Professor Shiller notes that students can take either or both, as they are designed to be self-contained.

questions.question: Professor Shiller views this course primarily as a vocational course for students planning careers in finance.
questions.explanation: The professor explicitly states that it is not primarily a vocational course, but an intellectual one.
questions.flashcard_back: No, it is an intellectual course about how things work.
questions.flashcard_explanation: The professor emphasizes the course is not just for those pursuing careers in finance.

questions.question: What is the primary difference in focus between Economics 251 and Economics 252 as described by the professor?
questions.answer: Economics 251 is more tuned into theoretical detail and mathematical rigor, while Economics 252 is designed to be accessible to those not comfortable with heavy math.
questions.explanation: The professor notes that John Geanakoplos is a mathematical economist and his course (251) is more tuned into theoretical detail.

questions.question: Why does Professor Shiller believe finance is important for students who do not plan to work in the financial sector?
questions.answer: He believes finance is a fundamental technology that underpins almost all human endeavors, and understanding it is necessary to understand how the real world works.
questions.explanation: The professor uses the example of a poet needing to understand the financial situation of publishers to illustrate that finance affects everyone.
